articles.title: Docker and Containerization: Image Design, Base Images and Compose vs Kubernetes
articles.scope: Expands the stub into a container-build guide: multi-stage builds, base-image choice (Alpine/musl vs Debian-slim/glibc vs distroless/chiseled vs scratch vs Docker Hardened Images, which ship dev and runtime variants), BuildKit caching, .NET SDK container publishing and Python/uv images, named volumes vs bind mounts, bridge vs host networking. Adds a CKAD image-task drill (build, tag, inspect, save/export to an OCI tarball and push with both docker and podman). Ends with the operational signals that justify moving from Docker Compose to Kubernetes (the decision itself is an ADR in decisions/). Engine and builder comparison lives in container-engines-and-image-builders; Windows images in windows-containers-for-dotnet-framework.

articles.title: OCI Images, Digests and Registries
articles.scope: Covers the OCI image, distribution and runtime specs: manifests, image indexes for multi-arch builds (pinned by index digest), layers, tags vs digests, and OCI 1.1 artifacts with the subject field and referrers API that attach signatures and SBOMs. Compares registry options (Docker Hub, GHCR, Harbor (CNCF graduated); ACR and ECR linked to provider folders) on retention, pull-through caching, tag immutability, geo-replication and image pull secrets.

articles.title: CI/CD Pipeline Design: Platforms, Stages, Artifacts and Promotion
articles.scope: The delivery hub. Compares GitHub Actions, Azure Pipelines, GitLab CI, Jenkins (CD Foundation), Tekton (CNCF incubating) and AWS CodePipeline (linked). Covers stage design, build-once-promote-everywhere, promotion across subscriptions and accounts (single- vs multi-account pipeline patterns), quality and release gates as a concept, pipeline health (failure rate, duration), cost and retention. Depth moves out: packages to ci-cd/package-management, testing to ci-cd/testing-in-ci-cd, versioning to ci-cd/versioning-and-release-management, branching to ci-cd/source-control-and-branching-strategies, deployments to ci-cd/deployment-strategies.

articles.title: Bare-Metal Linux, Hypervisors and the Certification Home Lab
articles.scope: Keeps the stub's comparisons: Type-1 vs Type-2 hypervisors (Proxmox VE, ESXi, KVM/libvirt), LXC system containers vs VMs vs Docker-on-VM, ZFS vs ext4/XFS, VLAN segmentation. Adds a reproducible multi-node kubeadm lab for CKA/CKS practice (kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta4 configuration, since v1beta3 was removed in v1.37), with lighter options (kind, k3s, Talos) as lab tools; choosing a production distribution is covered in kubernetes/kubernetes-distributions-compared.

articles.title: Platform Engineering: Internal Developer Platforms, Portals and Golden Paths
articles.scope: Conceptual page: platform-as-a-product, why a platform is not a portal (the developer portal is one surface of the IDP), golden paths and paved roads, Team Topologies platform teams, self-service with guardrails, and measuring platform success with DORA, SPACE and DevEx signals. Contrasts platform engineering with DevOps and SRE. Tool comparisons move out: self-service infrastructure to self-service-infrastructure-apis, a worked Backstage implementation to golden-path-end-to-end.

articles.title: GitHub Platform Foundations: Repositories, Collaboration and Administration
articles.scope: Covers Git vs GitHub; GitHub Desktop and GitHub Mobile; accounts, organizations, enterprises and Enterprise Managed Users; repository anatomy (README, LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING, CODEOWNERS, SECURITY), repository templates, insights, stars, feature previews and dependency insights; issues, pull requests, discussions, notifications, Gists, Wikis and Pages; Marketplace, Sponsors, following users and orgs, discoverable repositories, forks and InnerSource. Also roles, 2FA/passkeys, visibility, rulesets and org-wide Copilot policy. Maps the outline's legacy 'Copilot for Individuals, Business, and Enterprise' wording to today's plans: individual (Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max) vs Business vs Enterprise. Issues/Projects depth is in ci-cd/work-tracking-azure-boards-vs-github; Codespaces in dev-containers-and-cloud-development-environments; Git itself in ci-cd/git-in-depth.

articles.title: GitHub Copilot Surfaces and Features: IDE, Chat, Edits, Agent Mode, CLI, Cloud Agent, Code Review and Spaces
articles.scope: Owns GH-300:D2. Covers inline suggestions, chat, Copilot Edits, agent mode (with MCP tools), agent sessions and sub-agents, the Copilot CLI (install, commands, interactive and scripted sessions), Copilot cloud agent (formerly coding agent; copilot-setup-steps.yml, 59-minute session limit), Copilot code review with review instructions, PR summaries, Spaces, Spark (Pro+/Enterprise preview), the Copilot app and third-party agents (preview). Covers plans (Free, Student, Pro, Pro+, Max, Business, Enterprise) metered in GitHub AI Credits, with plan gating (content exclusion and org policy Business/Enterprise only; audit logs Pro+/Max/Business/Enterprise). Copilot-specific responsible use (validating suggestions, code referencing) is here; responsible-AI theory links to ai/foundations and security/ai-security, agent and MCP depth to ai/agents and ai/protocols.

articles.title: DevOps Foundations: Culture, CALMS, the Three Ways, SDLC Models and Value Streams
articles.scope: Defines DevOps and contrasts it with Agile, DevSecOps, SRE and platform engineering. Covers CALMS, the Three Ways, SDLC phases and models (waterfall, iterative, agile), value streams, WIP, lead time vs cycle time, feedback loops and shift left. Anchors the DORA, SRE and platform pages that contrast against it.

articles.title: Container Engines and Image Builders: Docker vs Podman vs nerdctl; BuildKit vs Buildah vs Cloud Native Buildpacks vs .NET SDK Container Publishing
articles.scope: Compares engines (Docker Engine, Podman, nerdctl on containerd) on daemon model, rootful vs rootless operation and Kubernetes fit, and builders (BuildKit/buildx, Buildah, Cloud Native Buildpacks (CNCF graduated), .NET SDK container publishing) on Dockerfile dependence, caching, multi-platform output and SBOM generation. Answers in-cluster builds now that Kaniko was archived on 2025-06-03.

articles.title: Windows Containers for .NET Framework Workloads: Base Images, Isolation Modes and Windows Node Pools
articles.scope: Containerizes .NET Framework apps that cannot run on Linux: Server Core vs Nano Server bases, process vs Hyper-V isolation, host/image version compatibility, gMSA for Active Directory auth, image size and patch cadence, and Windows nodes on AKS and EKS (linked). Links to architecture/migration for the rehost-vs-port decision.

articles.title: Dev Containers and Cloud Development Environments: devcontainer.json, Codespaces vs github.dev vs Microsoft Dev Box
articles.scope: Covers devcontainer.json (image or Dockerfile, features, extensions, ports, lifecycle scripts), setting up, customizing and using dev containers in Codespaces, how github.dev differs (browser editor, no compute), prebuilds and cost, and Microsoft Dev Box (linked to cloud/azure). Notes reuse in the Copilot cloud agent environment (copilot-setup-steps.yml).

articles.title: GitHub Copilot Data Flow, Privacy and Governance: Context Building, Proxy Filtering, Content Exclusions, Public-Code Filter, Policies and Audit
articles.scope: Covers how Copilot builds prompts from context, the proxy's filtering and post-processing, the suggestion lifecycle, data usage and retention, and LLM limits. Covers content exclusions and their documented limits (not honoured in VS Code Edit and Agent modes, IDE semantic information can leak, symlinks and remote filesystems not covered), the public-code filter and code referencing, output ownership, org and enterprise policies, audit-log events, REST API seat management and troubleshooting. Copilot-specific responsible use (validating output, human review) stays here; responsible-AI principles link to ai/foundations and security/ai-security.

articles.title: Prompt and Context Engineering with Copilot: Instructions, Prompt Files, Spaces and Productivity Use Cases
articles.scope: Applies prompting to Copilot: prompt structure, how context is chosen (open files, instructions, Spaces), zero-shot vs few-shot in chat, chat history, custom instructions vs prompt files. Works through generation, refactoring, documentation, sample data, legacy modernization, unit and integration tests, edge cases, and security and performance suggestions, with C# and Python examples. Generic prompting theory links to ai/applied.

articles.title: Building a Golden Path End to End: Backstage Software Template, Reusable Pipeline and Paved Runtime
articles.scope: Builds one golden path: a Backstage scaffolder template, catalog-info.yaml, TechDocs, a reusable workflow or extends template, a GitOps application on a paved Kubernetes runtime, and adoption and satisfaction metrics that treat the platform as a product.

articles.title: Self-Service Infrastructure APIs: Crossplane Compositions vs Terraform-Backed Catalogs (HCP No-Code Modules, Azure Deployment Environments, AWS Service Catalog)
articles.scope: Compares ways to publish governed infrastructure for self-service: Crossplane compositions and XRDs, HCP Terraform no-code modules, Azure Deployment Environments for on-demand self-deployment and AWS Service Catalog (both linked to provider folders), on API style, drift handling, guardrails and cost control.

articles.title: Kubernetes Architecture: Control Plane, Nodes and the Reconciliation Loop
articles.scope: Covers control plane vs nodes: kube-apiserver, etcd, kube-scheduler, kube-controller-manager, cloud-controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy and the container runtime (the old 'master' naming is retired in favour of control-plane). Explains the declarative API, labels and selectors, the reconciliation loop and the CRI/CNI/CSI extension interfaces, and what managed AKS/EKS take off your hands (linked).

articles.title: Workloads and Pod Lifecycle: Deployment vs StatefulSet vs DaemonSet vs Job, and Probes
articles.scope: Shows when to choose Pod, ReplicaSet, Deployment (rolling update, rollout undo), StatefulSet, DaemonSet, Job or CronJob (schedule, time zone, concurrency policy). Contrasts init containers, native sidecars (GA v1.33) and ephemeral containers, along with multi-container patterns, pod phases, restart policies, CrashLoopBackOff and graceful termination. Liveness vs readiness vs startup probes are shown with ASP.NET Core health checks and Python endpoints.

articles.title: ConfigMaps vs Secrets, and External Secret Stores
articles.scope: Compares env vars, mounted files and projected volumes (Secrets, ConfigMaps, downward API, bound tokens, ClusterTrustBundles), immutable objects and update propagation, and image pull secrets. Explains why base64 is not encryption and how encryption at rest works with KMS v2. Compares External Secrets Operator, the Secrets Store CSI Driver, Sealed Secrets and SOPS, with links to Azure Key Vault and AWS Secrets Manager.

articles.title: Scheduling and Resource Management: Requests, Limits, Affinity and Taints
articles.scope: Covers requests vs limits, QoS classes, LimitRange and ResourceQuota, pod-level resources (beta v1.34) and in-place pod resize (GA v1.35). Explains scheduler filtering and scoring, nodeSelector, node affinity, pod affinity and anti-affinity, taints and tolerations, topology spread constraints, PriorityClass and preemption, and PodDisruptionBudgets. Briefly contrasts device plugins with DRA (GA v1.34) and names the in-tree Workload/PodGroup API (scheduling.k8s.io/v1beta1 behind the GenericWorkload gate, beta and off by default in v1.37) vs Kueue and Volcano; depth is in ai-and-gpu-workloads-on-kubernetes.

articles.title: Kubernetes Networking Model, CNI Plugins and Cluster DNS
articles.scope: Explains the flat pod network model and compares CNI dataplanes (Calico, Cilium/eBPF, Flannel; Azure CNI and Amazon VPC CNI linked) across overlay, routed and cloud-native IPAM. Covers kube-proxy modes: iptables (default), nftables (GA v1.33, preferred on newer kernels) and IPVS (deprecated since v1.35; v1.37 adds the KubeProxyIPVS gate ahead of deactivation and removal), plus eBPF kube-proxy replacement. Teaches CoreDNS (1.14.x in v1.37) service discovery, with kube-dns as legacy history.

articles.title: Services, Ingress and Gateway API
articles.scope: Compares ClusterIP, NodePort, LoadBalancer, ExternalName and headless Services, and explains EndpointSlices (the Endpoints API is deprecated since v1.33). Contrasts the Ingress resource and Ingress controllers with Gateway API (GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, ReferenceGrant) and its role separation; HTTPRoute and GRPCRoute are standard-channel, TCPRoute/UDPRoute experimental, and mesh support comes through GAMMA. Covers TLS termination with cert-manager. The Ingress NGINX retirement (no releases or security fixes after March 2026) and migration steps are in migrating-ingress-nginx-to-gateway-api.

articles.title: NetworkPolicies: Default Deny, Egress and CNI Enforcement
articles.scope: Builds default-deny, ingress and egress rules with pod/namespace selectors and ipBlocks, and covers DNS egress gotchas. Explains that enforcement depends on the CNI, how Cilium/Calico extended policies add to it, and the SIG Network Policy API's ClusterNetworkPolicy (Admin and Baseline tiers; an out-of-tree CRD implemented by only some CNIs, successor to AdminNetworkPolicy/BaselineAdminNetworkPolicy). Covers how to test policies and contrasts L3/L4 policy with L7 mesh authorization.

articles.title: Kubernetes Storage: Volumes, PV/PVC, StorageClasses and CSI
articles.scope: Covers ephemeral volumes (emptyDir including medium Memory, generic ephemeral volumes, projected volumes, image volumes GA v1.36 for read-only OCI artifacts such as models) vs persistent volumes; static vs dynamic provisioning through StorageClasses and CSI drivers; access modes (RWO, ROX, RWX, RWOP); reclaim policies; expansion; VolumeAttributesClass (GA v1.34); CSI VolumeSnapshots; StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates; and hostPath as a privilege-escalation vector blocked by the Baseline Pod Security Standard. Links to Azure Disk/Files and EBS/EFS CSI pages.

articles.title: Authentication, Authorization and RBAC in Kubernetes
articles.scope: Contrasts authentication (X.509 client certificates, OIDC/JWT, ServiceAccount tokens) with authorization (RBAC, Node, webhook). Covers structured authentication configuration (GA v1.34, multiple JWT issuers), structured authorization configuration (GA v1.32), the Node authorizer with NodeRestriction, the CSR API for user certificates, kubectl auth whoami and can-i, Role vs ClusterRole and their bindings, aggregation, bound projected tokens, kubeconfig and exec credential plugins (client security), and least-privilege patterns. Links to AKS Entra integration and EKS access entries.

articles.title: Admission Control: Webhooks, CEL Policies, Kyverno and Gatekeeper
articles.scope: Walks the admission chain (mutating, schema validation, validating). Compares admission webhooks with CEL-based ValidatingAdmissionPolicy (GA v1.30) and MutatingAdmissionPolicy (GA v1.36), and Kyverno (CNCF graduated) with OPA Gatekeeper. Covers failure policies, the availability risk of webhooks, and audit-then-enforce rollout.

articles.title: Pod Security Standards, Pod Security Admission and securityContext
articles.scope: Covers the Privileged/Baseline/Restricted levels and the enforce/audit/warn namespace labels, with PodSecurityPolicy (removed in v1.25) as history. Hardens Pods field by field (runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, allowPrivilegeEscalation, dropped Linux capabilities, seccomp RuntimeDefault, AppArmor, SELinux) and adds user namespaces (GA v1.36), contrasted with rootless container engines.

articles.title: Helm vs Kustomize: Templating vs Patching
articles.scope: Compares Helm 4 (charts vs releases, values, hooks, OCI distribution, rollback, server-side apply) with Kustomize (bases, overlays, patches, components). Shows how to combine them through post-render plugins or Kustomize helmCharts, and how Argo CD and Flux consume each.

articles.title: Extending Kubernetes: CRDs, Controllers and the Operator Pattern
articles.scope: Covers CRD schemas, CEL validation rules, versioning and conversion, controllers and the reconcile loop, finalizers, operator capability levels, and discovering, installing and configuring operators (the CKA/CKAD depth). A clearly labelled expert section compares building operators with Kubebuilder/Operator SDK (Go), KubeOps (.NET) and Kopf (Python).

articles.title: Autoscaling: HPA vs VPA vs KEDA vs Cluster Autoscaler vs Karpenter
articles.scope: Contrasts workload autoscaling (HPA v2 behaviour; configurable tolerance GA in v1.37; scale-to-zero beta and on by default in v1.37 for object and external metrics; VPA including its in-place update mode built on in-place resize; KEDA event-driven scaling; Knative Serving request-driven scale-to-zero) with node autoscaling (Cluster Autoscaler node groups vs Karpenter NodePools, a Kubernetes SIG Autoscaling project). Covers the Metrics API pipeline (metrics.k8s.io/v1 in v1.37 via metrics-server) and how autoscaling interacts with requests, PDBs and in-place resize. Links to AKS node auto-provisioning and EKS Auto Mode.

articles.title: Troubleshooting Kubernetes: A Repeatable Triage Method
articles.scope: Gives decision trees for Pending, CrashLoopBackOff, ImagePullBackOff, OOMKilled, failing probes, stuck Terminating (finalizers), and Service, DNS or NetworkPolicy faults, using kubectl describe/logs/events/top/debug and ephemeral containers. Covers node and control-plane debugging with kubelet logs, journalctl, crictl, static Pod manifests and certificate expiry.

articles.title: Cluster Lifecycle: kubeadm, HA Control Planes, Upgrades and etcd Backup
articles.scope: Covers kubeadm init/join with kubeadm.k8s.io/v1beta4 ClusterConfiguration/InitConfiguration (v1beta3 was removed in v1.37; use kubeadm config migrate), stacked vs external etcd, HA control planes and the version skew policy. Walks the upgrade sequence (cordon, drain with PDBs, kubeadm upgrade), etcd 3.6 backup with etcdctl snapshot save and restore with etcdutl snapshot restore, kubeadm certs check-expiration and renew, and CSR-based user certificates, and contrasts this with managed upgrade channels on AKS and EKS. API deprecations are in kubernetes-api-and-declarative-management; workload backup in kubernetes-backup-and-disaster-recovery.

articles.title: The Kubernetes Security Model: 4Cs, Trust Boundaries and Threats
articles.scope: Uses the 4Cs and cluster trust boundaries and data flows to walk the KCSA threat categories: persistence, denial of service, malicious code, network attackers, sensitive-data access and privilege escalation. Covers each component's attack surface and maps Kubernetes onto compliance and threat frameworks (CIS Benchmark, NSA/CISA Kubernetes Hardening Guide, the MITRE ATT&CK containers matrix and the Kubernetes threat matrix) with automation tooling (Kubescape, kube-bench, Trivy Operator). Framework definitions link to security/grc, security/threat-modeling (STRIDE) and security/detection-response.

articles.title: Cluster and System Hardening: CIS Benchmark to Host OS
articles.scope: Covers kube-bench against the CIS Benchmark and Kubescape against NSA/CISA and MITRE, API server exposure and authentication flags, kubelet hardening with NodeRestriction, node metadata protection, audit policy, etcd encryption, binary verification and upgrades as a security control. Adds host-OS minimization, least-privilege IAM, firewalling and AppArmor/seccomp/SELinux profiles.

articles.title: Supply Chain Security for Kubernetes: Scan, Sign, Verify, Admit
articles.scope: Covers minimal base images, image scanning (Trivy, Grype), static analysis (kubesec, KubeLinter), SBOMs (SPDX, CycloneDX), signing with Sigstore cosign vs Notation, registry controls (Harbor, private registries, image pull secrets) and admission enforcement of permitted registries and signatures (Kyverno verifyImages, Gatekeeper with Ratify). Links to security/supply-chain for SLSA and SBOM theory and to ci-cd/github-supply-chain-security for the GitHub side.

articles.title: Runtime Security: Falco, Audit Logs and Container Immutability
articles.scope: Compares Falco's syscall/eBPF behavioural detection (CNCF graduated) with Tetragon in-kernel enforcement, and audit logs with runtime events. Covers container immutability at runtime, investigating attack phases, and forwarding detections to SIEM (links to Microsoft Sentinel and GuardDuty EKS protection).

articles.title: Multi-Tenancy and Workload Isolation: Namespaces to Sandboxed Runtimes
articles.scope: Compares soft and hard multi-tenancy: namespace-per-team with RBAC, quotas and policies vs virtual clusters vs cluster-per-tenant. Covers node isolation with pools and taints, container runtimes (containerd, CRI-O, runc), and sandboxed runtimes via RuntimeClass (gVisor, Kata Containers) with their cost and blast radius.

articles.title: Service Mesh and Pod-to-Pod Encryption: Sidecar, Ambient and eBPF
articles.scope: Explains why meshes exist and compares Istio sidecar vs Istio ambient (ztunnel, waypoints) vs Linkerd vs Cilium's sidecarless mesh. Covers mTLS workload identity (and in-tree Pod certificates as an alternative source), traffic shifting and retries, CNI-level WireGuard/IPsec vs mesh mTLS, Gateway API for mesh (GAMMA), and the operating cost.

articles.title: The Cloud Native Ecosystem: CNCF Governance, Project Maturity, Open Standards and the Kubernetes Community
articles.scope: Covers cloud native principles, the CNCF TOC and TAGs, Sandbox/Incubating/Graduated maturity levels, Kubernetes SIGs, KEPs, release cadence and support windows, Certified Kubernetes conformance (including the AI conformance program), open standards (OCI, CRI, CNI, CSI, CloudEvents, OpenTelemetry), serverless on Kubernetes with Knative, and how to contribute.

articles.title: The Kubernetes API: Groups and Versions, Deprecation Policy, Server-Side Apply and Declarative vs Imperative kubectl
articles.scope: Covers API groups and versions, the deprecation policy and windows, kubectl convert and explain, the version skew policy, managedFields and server-side apply (which Helm 4 and GitOps rely on), apply vs create vs replace, imperative generators, and KYAML output (kubectl get -o kyaml, stable in v1.37).

articles.title: Kubernetes PKI and Certificates: Cluster CA, kubeadm Certificates, CSR API, cert-manager, ClusterTrustBundles and Pod Certificates
articles.scope: Maps the cluster, front-proxy and etcd CAs and every component certificate; kubeadm certs check-expiration and renew; user certificates through the CSR API; kubeconfig client security; cert-manager (CNCF graduated) for Ingress and Gateway TLS; and ClusterTrustBundles and Pod certificates (both GA in v1.37) for workload mTLS.

articles.title: Migrating from Ingress NGINX to Gateway API
articles.scope: A 2026 migration task: Ingress NGINX gets no releases, bug fixes or security fixes after March 2026. Inventories annotations, converts with ingress2gateway, maps rewrites, TLS, canary weights and traffic splitting to HTTPRoute features, and compares alternative Ingress controllers for teams not ready for Gateway API.

articles.title: Kubernetes Backup and Disaster Recovery: etcd Snapshots vs Velero vs GitOps Rebuild
articles.scope: Contrasts control-plane recovery from etcd snapshots with workload and PV backup (Velero, CSI VolumeSnapshots), managed-cluster backup on AKS and EKS (linked) and rebuild-from-Git, on RTO/RPO, scope and restore testing. Links to architecture/reliability for RTO/RPO design.

articles.title: Multi-Cluster Kubernetes: Cluster API, Fleet Management and Cross-Cluster Networking
articles.scope: Covers why and when to run many clusters, Cluster API declarative lifecycle, Karmada (CNCF graduated), Argo CD and Flux fleets, Cilium Cluster Mesh, the Multi-Cluster Services API and global load balancing for HA, with AKS Fleet Manager and EKS options linked.

articles.title: Developer Inner Loop on Kubernetes: kind/k3d, Skaffold, Tilt, Telepresence or mirrord, and Aspire
articles.scope: The daily workflow for the .NET/Python reader: local clusters (kind, k3d) vs remote development, rebuild-and-redeploy loops with Skaffold and Tilt, port-forward vs traffic interception (Telepresence, mirrord), and Aspire (formerly .NET Aspire) local orchestration and publishing to Kubernetes.

articles.title: AI and GPU Workloads on Kubernetes: Device Plugins, DRA, Kueue, Gang Scheduling and Inference Routing
articles.scope: Covers device plugins vs Dynamic Resource Allocation (GA v1.34), the in-tree Workload/PodGroup API (scheduling.k8s.io/v1beta1, GenericWorkload gate, beta and off by default in v1.37; v1alpha2 objects must be deleted before upgrade), Kueue and Volcano for queueing and gang scheduling, image volumes for model artifacts (GA v1.36), the Gateway API Inference Extension and the Kubernetes AI Conformance program. KServe, vLLM and managed AI services link to ai/platforms.

articles.title: Kubernetes Cost Allocation and Rightsizing: Requests-Based Showback, OpenCost and Bin-Packing
articles.scope: Ties requests and limits, VPA and in-place resize, Karpenter consolidation and bin-packing to namespace and label showback with OpenCost (CNCF incubating), and to idle-cost and shared-cost allocation. Links to architecture/cost and cloud/*/cost.

articles.title: Kubernetes Distributions: Upstream kubeadm vs k3s, RKE2, Talos and OpenShift, and When to Prefer Managed AKS/EKS
articles.scope: An architect's distribution choice: conformance, support windows, security defaults (SELinux, immutable OS), upgrade tooling and operations cost of kubeadm, k3s, RKE2, Talos and OpenShift, and the signals that favour managed AKS or EKS. AKS vs EKS stays in cloud/compare.

articles.title: IaC Fundamentals: Declarative vs Imperative, Provisioning vs Configuration
articles.scope: Contrasts IaC with click-ops and scripts. Covers declarative vs imperative, provisioning vs configuration management, mutable vs immutable infrastructure, idempotency and drift. Maps the tool landscape (Terraform/OpenTofu, Bicep, CloudFormation/CDK, Pulumi, Crossplane) with links to provider folders and to the deeper comparison pages (configuration-management-compared, iac-in-general-purpose-languages).

articles.title: Terraform Language and Core Workflow
articles.scope: Covers providers, version constraints and the dependency lock file (.terraform.lock.hcl), multiple provider configurations with aliases, resource vs data blocks, variables, locals and outputs, complex types, expressions and functions, meta-arguments (count, for_each, depends_on, lifecycle), dynamic blocks, dependencies and custom conditions (validation, preconditions, check blocks). Walks init, validate, plan, apply, destroy and fmt with side-by-side azurerm and aws examples. The exam covers Terraform 1.12; actions and list blocks with terraform query are tagged 'beyond TF-A 004'. Secrets handling is in terraform-secrets-and-vault.

articles.title: Terraform State, Backends, Locking and Drift
articles.scope: Covers what state stores and why, local vs remote backends (azurerm blob leases, s3 native lockfiles), state locking, and why HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise use the cloud block rather than a backend (the remote backend is legacy). Covers drift with refresh-only plans, import blocks vs the terraform import command, moved and removed blocks, state CLI commands and TF_LOG verbose logging, and contrasts OpenTofu client-side state encryption. Secrets in state are covered in terraform-secrets-and-vault.

articles.title: Terraform Modules, Composition and Environment Strategies
articles.scope: Covers module sources and version pinning, the public Terraform Registry and HCP private registry, variable scope and composition patterns. Compares environment strategies (separate directories vs CLI workspaces vs HCP workspaces and projects vs Terraform Stacks, tagged 'beyond TF-A 004') and repository layouts for multi-subscription and multi-account estates.

articles.title: Terraform vs OpenTofu
articles.scope: Compares licensing (BSL 1.1 vs MPL 2.0) and governance (HashiCorp, an IBM company, vs a CNCF Sandbox project under the Linux Foundation since April 2025). Tracks feature divergence: OpenTofu state encryption, provider for_each, OCI registry distribution and early evaluation vs Terraform Stacks, actions, list blocks with terraform query and Terraform Policy (GA in the CLI from v1.17.0). Covers registries, compatibility and decision criteria; OpenTofu is not in the TF-A objectives, so the page is context rather than exam content.

articles.title: HCP Terraform and Running IaC in Pipelines
articles.scope: Covers HCP Terraform organizations, projects and workspaces connected through the cloud block; VCS-, CLI- and API-driven runs; variable sets, dynamic provider credentials (OIDC to Azure, AWS and Vault), run tasks, policy sets (Sentinel and OPA apply to workspaces only; Terraform Policy, documented as beta in HCP Terraform, applies to workspaces and Stacks), agents, the private registry and Stacks (beyond TF-A 004). Contrasts Terraform Enterprise (self-hosted) and running Terraform in GitHub Actions or Azure Pipelines and with Atlantis, Spacelift and env0.

articles.title: Policy as Code for Infrastructure: OPA, Checkov, Sentinel and Terraform Policy
